description: Fix confirmed bugs, apply hardening improvements, and bring player experience to iOS parity on the web dashboard (landing/dashboard/). Bug fixes (credit calc, ticket detail security, attention feed), quality-of-life (explicit filters, parlay badge, UUID validation, edge function timeout, parlay leg filters), and player UX (games as default tab, sport pages with league sub-tabs + futures, track tab for standalone, time filters). All changes in landing/dashboard/ files: dashboard.js, app.html, dashboard.css. CRITICAL: The iOS app (Booki/ directory) is the reference implementation. Before building any web feature, READ the corresponding iOS Swift code. Key references: GamesView.swift (player games tab), SportPageView.swift (sport hub with league tabs), SportCategory.swift (sport/league enum), TrackView.swift (player picks).

userStories.title: Fix credit calculation to not penalize winning players
userStories.description: As a player, my available credit should increase when I'm winning (negative balance), not decrease. The current Math.abs() penalizes winning players identically to losing players.
acceptanceCriteria: In playerCreditUtilization getter (~line 725), change Math.abs(this.playerBalance) to Math.max(0, this.playerBalance)
In playerAvailableCredit getter (~line 731), change Math.abs(this.playerBalance) to Math.max(0, this.playerBalance)
A player with -$500 balance (bookie owes them), $1000 credit limit, $200 open stakes should have: availableCredit = max(0, 1000 - max(0, -500) - 200) = $800, NOT $300
A player with +$500 balance (owes bookie), $1000 credit limit, $200 open stakes should have: availableCredit = max(0, 1000 - 500 - 200) = $300
Credit utilization percentage should use same formula: (max(0, balance) + openStakes) / creditLimit * 100
Reference: iOS BalanceService.swift line 60: creditLimit - stakes - owed (raw balance, no abs)
userStories.notes: iOS formula at BalanceService.swift:60 is `creditLimit - stakes - owed` where owed is the raw ledger sum. CLAUDE.md says max(0, balance). Either way, Math.abs is wrong — winning players should NOT have reduced credit.

userStories.title: Add player_id filter to ticket detail query
userStories.description: As a player, I should only be able to view my own bets. The current ticket detail query fetches any bet by ID without ownership check.
acceptanceCriteria: In loadPlayerTicketDetail() (~line 943), add .eq('player_id', this.playerId) to the Supabase query chain after .eq('id', this.selectedBetId)
If the query returns 0 rows (bet doesn't belong to player), show toast 'Failed to load pick' and return early
This is a defense-in-depth measure — RLS also protects, but explicit filters are best practice
Test: navigating to #/player-ticket/{someone-elses-bet-id} should show error toast, not the bet
userStories.notes: RLS on bets table already restricts to own bets via player_id = get_player_id(), but explicit filtering is defense-in-depth and optimizes query planning.

userStories.title: Fix attention feed credit utilization to include open stakes
userStories.description: As an organizer, the Near Limit alerts and Risk Watchlist should factor in open stakes, not just balance. A player with $0 balance but $900 in open stakes on a $1000 limit should trigger the 75% alert.
acceptanceCriteria: In dashboardMembers mapping (~line 1807), ensure openStakes is included: openStakes: memberExposureMap[p.id]?.openStakes || 0
In memberExposureMap building (~line 1794), track openStakes per member: add openStakes to the map object, increment by Number(b.stake) for each open bet

In dashboardAlerts getter, Near Credit Limit section (~line 1927): change utilization formula from Math.abs(m.balance || 0) / limit * 100 to (Math.max(0, m.balance || 0) + (m.openStakes || 0)) / limit * 100
In riskWatchlist getter (~line 1983): apply same utilization formula fix
Both formulas must use Math.max(0, balance) not Math.abs(balance) — consistent with US-001 fix
Reference: iOS BalanceService.playerSummary() includes openStakes in credit utilization
userStories.notes: The memberExposureMap already tracks exposure (potential payouts) and openPicks per member. Adding openStakes (sum of stakes) follows the same pattern. iOS BalanceService.playerSummary() bundles openStakes into credit utilization.

userStories.title: Add explicit bookie_id filter to organizer pick detail and parlay leg queries
userStories.description: As an organizer, pick detail and parlay leg queries should explicitly filter by bookie_id for clarity and query optimization, even though RLS already enforces isolation.
acceptanceCriteria: In loadPickDetail() (~line 2674), add .eq('bookie_id', this.bookie.id) to the bets query after .eq('id', this.selectedBetId)
In the parlay legs fetch within loadPickDetail() (~line 2710), add .eq('bookie_id', this.bookie.id) to the query after .eq('ticket_id', ...)
Both changes are defense-in-depth — RLS already blocks cross-bookie access
Verify loadPickDetail still works: navigate to pick detail from picks tab, confirm bet data loads correctly
Verify parlay legs still load: navigate to a multi-pick detail, confirm all legs display
userStories.notes: Other organizer queries already use explicit bookie_id filters (e.g., loadMemberDetail at line 2576). These two queries are outliers. Adding the filter improves query planning and makes intent explicit.

userStories.title: Suppress parlay partial badge when parlay has a losing leg
userStories.description: As a user viewing a multi-pick, if any leg has lost, the parlay should show a normal 'Lost' appearance instead of 'Partial (X/Y)' — matching iOS behavior.
acceptanceCriteria: Read iOS TrackView.swift and TicketDetailView.swift to understand the exact parlay badge suppression logic

In the pick card rendering (both organizer picks list and player track view), when displaying a parlay bet's status: if any leg has status 'lost' or 'graded' with a losing result, show 'Lost' badge (badge-danger) instead of 'Partial (X/Y)'
The 'Partial' badge should only show when all resolved legs are wins and some legs are still pending
For organizer pick detail view (loadPickDetail), apply same logic to the status display in the hero card
For player ticket detail view (loadPlayerTicketDetail), apply same logic
A parlay with 3 legs where 1 won and 1 lost should show 'Lost', not 'Partial (1/3)' or 'Partial (2/3)'
Reference: CLAUDE.md says 'Suppressed Partial (X/Y) badge and will lose warning when parlay already has a losing leg — shows normal Lost appearance'
userStories.notes: This is a cosmetic fix matching iOS behavior documented in CLAUDE.md. The key insight: once any leg loses, the parlay outcome is determined (lost), so showing 'Partial' is misleading.

userStories.title: Add UUID validation to hash route parsing
userStories.description: As a user, navigating to an invalid route like #/picks/not-a-uuid should redirect to the parent view instead of sending garbage IDs to the database.
acceptanceCriteria: Add a isValidUUID(str) helper function that validates UUID v4 format: /^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$/i
In parseRoute(), after each regex match (memberMatch, pickMatch, eventMatch, playerTicketMatch), validate the captured ID with isValidUUID() before setting the route
If UUID is invalid, redirect to the parent route: invalid member ID → #/members, invalid pick ID → #/picks, invalid event ID → #/events, invalid player-ticket ID → #/player-track
Do NOT show an error toast for invalid UUIDs — just silently redirect
Valid UUIDs in both uppercase and lowercase should be accepted (the regex uses case-insensitive flag)
Test: #/picks/abc → redirects to #/picks, #/picks/f3ad0fa1-1234-5678-9abc-def012345678 → loads pick detail
userStories.notes: This prevents unnecessary database queries with invalid IDs. Currently these fail gracefully (toast error), but silent redirect is cleaner UX. The helper can be reused elsewhere.

userStories.title: Add timeout and retry to callEdgeFunction
userStories.description: As a user, edge function calls should timeout after 10 seconds instead of hanging indefinitely, and show user-friendly error messages.
acceptanceCriteria: In callEdgeFunction(), wrap the fetch call with an AbortController and 10-second timeout
If the request times out (AbortError), throw an error with message 'Request timed out. Please try again.'
If the response is not ok AND has no error field in body, throw with a more descriptive message than just 'HTTP 500' — include the function name: 'Failed to call {name}. Please try again.'
If fetch throws a network error (TypeError from fetch), catch it and throw 'Network error. Check your connection and try again.'
Do NOT add retry logic — keep it simple, let the user retry manually
Ensure the AbortController is properly cleaned up (clearTimeout) in both success and error paths
Reference: iOS EdgeFunctionService.swift has retry logic, but for web a timeout is sufficient
userStories.notes: Keep this simple — just a timeout and better error messages. No retry logic needed since the user can retry manually. The iOS app has retry logic in EdgeFunctionService.swift but the web dashboard is simpler.

userStories.title: Add explicit player_id filter to parlay leg queries in player ticket detail
userStories.description: As a player viewing a multi-pick detail, the parlay leg query should explicitly filter by player_id for defense-in-depth.
acceptanceCriteria: In loadPlayerTicketDetail() parlay legs fetch (~line 960), add .eq('player_id', this.playerId) to the query after .eq('ticket_id', ...)
This ensures only the current player's parlay legs are returned, matching the player_id filter already added in US-002 for the main bet query
Verify multi-pick detail still works: navigate to a multi-pick from player track, confirm all legs display correctly
This is defense-in-depth — RLS already restricts to own bets
userStories.notes: Complements US-002 (which added player_id to the main bet query). The parlay legs query should have the same filter for consistency.

The current Home tab content (balance, record, recent activity) should move into a persistent header or into the Account tab.
acceptanceCriteria: Read iOS PlayerMainView.swift and GamesView.swift to understand the player tab structure — GAMES is tab 0, the primary landing
Remove the 'Home' sidebar link and the player-home route entirely

In playerRoutes array (line 435), replace 'player-home' with 'player-games' as the first entry, remove 'player-home'

Move the key Home tab content into a persistent balance header on the Games page: show player display balance (formatted currency with Credit/You owe/Settled label) and available credit in a compact bar above the sport filter chips
The balance header should match the iOS PlayerTabView pattern: balance on the left, available credit on the right, single row, subtle background (var(--card-bg))
Move performance stats (record, open picks count) and recent activity into the Account tab — add a 'Performance' card at the top of player-account showing W-L-P record and open picks count

userStories.notes: iOS PlayerMainView.swift line 60: Tab('GAMES', systemImage: 'house.fill', value: 0). Games is THE player home. The separate Home tab with balance summary is a web-only pattern that doesn't match iOS. Balance info should be persistent (visible from Games) not a separate tab. Reference: iOS PlayerTabView wraps each tab with a header showing balance.

Outright markets have market_type='outright' in the markets table.
